project.name: cavet
project.description: A Go CLI security-triage tool for coding agents. It runs scanners (trivy, opengrep, gitleaks, checkov) inside an offline container engine and records every finding and decision in an append-only audit log.
project.note: This finding comes from a scan of the cavet repository itself.

findings.description:

User controlled data in methods like `innerHTML`, `outerHTML` or `document.write` is an anti-pattern that can lead to XSS vulnerabilities

findings.description:
engine/Dockerfile:146
engine/Dockerfile:154
engine/Dockerfile:170
By not specifying a USER, a program in the container may run as 'root'. This is a security hazard. If an attacker can control a process running as root, they may have control over the container. Ensure that the last USER in a Dockerfile is a USER other than 'root'.
verdict: confirmed (high confidence, by operator): final-core stage (FROM rules at engine/Dockerfile:141) has no USER before its HEALTHCHECK/ENTRYPOINT, so the scanner image runs as root; the CLI's --user override applies only on linux builds (internal/engineclient/client.go:139-141), leaving root as the effective user on Windows/Docker Desktop

verdict: confirmed (high confidence, by operator): final-core stage (FROM rules at engine/Dockerfile:141) has no USER before its HEALTHCHECK/ENTRYPOINT, so the scanner image runs as root; the CLI's --user override applies only on linux builds (internal/engineclient/client.go:139-141), leaving root as the effective user on Windows/Docker Desktop

findings.description:
engine/Dockerfile:147
engine/Dockerfile:155
engine/Dockerfile:171
By not specifying a USER, a program in the container may run as 'root'. This is a security hazard. If an attacker can control a process running as root, they may have control over the container. Ensure that the last USER in a Dockerfile is a USER other than 'root'.
verdict: confirmed (high confidence, by operator): the entrypoint at engine/Dockerfile:155 runs under the stage default of root because final-core sets no USER; only linux-built CLI invocations override it (internal/engineclient/client.go:139-141), so the entrypoint executes as root in normal use on the primary platform

  130 |     printf 'resource "aws_s3_bucket" "b" {}\n' > /seed/main.tf; \
  131 |     trivy fs --scanners misconfig --skip-db-update /seed || true; \
  132 |     rm -rf /seed; \
  133 |     test -d /opt/trivy-cache/policy/content
  134 | 
  135 | FROM trivy-data-core AS trivy-data-full

findings.description:
engine/Dockerfile:147
engine/Dockerfile:155
engine/Dockerfile:171
By not specifying a USER, a program in the container may run as 'root'. This is a security hazard. If an attacker can control a process running as root, they may have control over the container. Ensure that the last USER in a Dockerfile is a USER other than 'root'.

A gitleaks generic-api-key was detected which attempts to identify hard-coded credentials. It is not recommended to store credentials in source-code, as this risks secrets being leaked and used by either an internal or external malicious adversary. It is recommended to use environment variables to securely provide credentials or retrieve credentials from a secure vault or HSM (Hardware Security Module). This rule can introduce a lot of false positives, it is not recommended to be used in PR comments.

findings.description:
To ensure reproducible builds, pin Dockerfile `FROM` commands to a specific hash. You can find the hash by running `docker pull debian` and then specify it with `debian:bookworm-slim@sha256:<hash goes here>`
verdict: dismissed (high confidence, by operator): floating the debian:bookworm-slim tag is deliberate and documented in the Dockerfile itself (lines 16-17): a digest-pinned base would freeze a stale apt snapshot, so the build runs apt-get -y upgrade to pull security updates instead; the golang builder stages remain digest-pinned (lines 41, 63)

project.name: cavet
project.description: A Go CLI security-triage tool for coding agents. It runs scanners (trivy, opengrep, gitleaks, checkov) inside an offline container engine and records every finding and decision in an append-only audit log.
project.note: This finding comes from a scan of the cavet repository itself.

internal/engineclient/image.go:162
Detected file permissions that are set to more than `0600` (user/owner can read and write). Setting file permissions to higher than `0600` is most likely unnecessary and violates the principle of least privilege. Instead, set permissions to be `0600` or less for os.Chmod, os.Mkdir, os.OpenFile, os.MkdirAll, and ioutil.WriteFile

Detected file permissions that are set to more than `0600` (user/owner can read and write). Setting file permissions to higher than `0600` is most likely unnecessary and violates the principle of least privilege. findings.description:
engine/Dockerfile:65
'RUN cd ...' to change directory
verdict: dismissed (high confidence, by operator): cd /src at engine/Dockerfile:43 is chained inside a single RUN whose entire body operates under /src; the gitleaks-build stage contains no later RUN that could assume a persisted working directory, so the hazard DS-0013 flags does not arise (same shape in trivy-build)

findings.source_excerpt:
37 | # tag plus go's own module-hash verification (checksum db) cover provenance.
   38 | # gore2regex + CGO_ENABLED=0 mirror the upstream release build (go-re2 is
   39 | # pure-Go wazero, no cgo needed); -ldflags injects the version so
   40 | # `gitleaks --version` still reports the tag.
   41 | FROM golang:1.26-bookworm@sha256:9fdc884aacc3bec89b20ffc69f4bb369c78210e3e4f600387b5128b12c199f81 AS gitleaks-build
   42 | ARG GITLEAKS_VERSION
   43 | RUN git clone --depth 1 --branch "v${GITLEAKS_VERSION}" https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks /src \
   44 |     && cd /src \
   45 |     && go get golang.org/x/crypto@latest golang.org/x/net@latest \
   46 |     && go mod tidy \
   47 |     && CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -tags gore2regex -trimpath \
   48 |         -ldflags "-s -w -X=github.com/zricethezav/gitleaks/v8/version.Version=${GITLEAKS_VERSION}" \
   49 |         -o /out/gitleaks .

findings.description:
internal/serve/assets/app.js:506

project.name: cavet
project.description: A Go CLI security-triage tool for coding agents. It runs scanners (trivy, opengrep, gitleaks, checkov) inside an offline container engine and records every finding and decision in an append-only audit log.
project.note: This finding comes from a scan of the cavet repository itself.

findings.description:
engine/Dockerfile:65
'RUN cd ...' to change directory
verdict: dismissed (high confidence, by operator): cd /src at engine/Dockerfile:43 is chained inside a single RUN whose entire body operates under /src; the gitleaks-build stage contains no later RUN that could assume a persisted working directory, so the hazard DS-0013 flags does not arise (same shape in trivy-build)
findings.path_class: container image build definition (shipped as the scanner engine image)
findings.source_excerpt:
37 | # tag plus go's own module-hash verification (checksum db) cover provenance.
   38 | # gore2regex + CGO_ENABLED=0 mirror the upstream release build (go-re2 is
   39 | # pure-Go wazero, no cgo needed); -ldflags injects the version so
   40 | # `gitleaks --version` still reports the tag.
   41 | FROM golang:1.26-bookworm@sha256:9fdc884aacc3bec89b20ffc69f4bb369c78210e3e4f600387b5128b12c199f81 AS gitleaks-build
   42 | ARG GITLEAKS_VERSION
   43 | RUN git clone --depth 1 --branch "v${GITLEAKS_VERSION}" https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks /src \
   44 |     && cd /src \
   45 |     && go get golang.org/x/crypto@latest golang.org/x/net@latest \
   46 |     && go mod tidy \
   47 |     && CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -tags gore2regex -trimpath \
   48 |         -ldflags "-s -w -X=github.com/zricethezav/gitleaks/v8/version.Version=${GITLEAKS_VERSION}" \
   49 |         -o /out/gitleaks .

findings.description:
Detected file permissions that are set to more than `0600` (user/owner can read and write). Setting file permissions to higher than `0600` is most likely unnecessary and violates the principle of least privilege. Instead, set permissions to be `0600` or less for os.Chmod, os.Mkdir, os.OpenFile, os.MkdirAll, and ioutil.WriteFile
verdict: dismissed (high confidence, by operator): internal/cli/hook.go:15 mkdir 0755 and the hook shims at 0755 are deliberate: git only executes hooks carrying the executable bit, and the shim content is a fixed two-line cavet scan invocation with no secrets; 0755 grants write only to the owner

Detected file permissions that are set to more than `0600` (user/owner can read and write).
